questions.question: What is the key additional step used to handle higher-dimensional or singular subschemes, where earlier arguments had relied on smooth zero-dimensional loci?

options.A: Find a smooth closed Hecke-equivariant subscheme ZK within YK by intersecting the smallest length stratum and repeatedly removing nonsmooth points
options.B: Replace every subscheme by its normalization and ignore Hecke actions
options.C: Assume the conormal sequence is locally free for all YK

options.A: There may be no nowhere-vanishing Hecke-invariant section, and the conormal sequence need not be exact or locally free
options.B: The Hecke algebra ceases to act on coherent cohomology
options.C: The Hodge line bundle is undefined on every singular scheme
options.D: The Shimura variety has no prime-to-p Hecke operators
